newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cheung Kong Inf tops 1996 results target.
newsitem.headline: Cheung Kong Inf tops 1996 results target.

text.p: Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd (CKI) reported net profit of HK$886 million in 1996, well above the forecast of HK$728 million made when the company listed last June, chairman Victor Li said on Thursday.
The 1996 performance also was a 56 percent increase over the company's pro forma results for 1995, he said.
Profit contribution from infrastructure businesses increased 51 percent from last year, and the infrastructure materials businesses posted 41 percent growth.
"Our business is infrastructure, and the challenge is to capture opportunities in China's infrastructure sector," Li said.
In 1996, 69 percent of net profit was derived from the company's building materials operations, chiefly Green Island Cement Holdings Ltd and Anderson Asia Ltd, based in Hong Kong.
The remaining 31 percent was from transportation and energy infrastructure projects in China.
When the company listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange, it had a portfolio of 19 infrastructural development projects in China -- 13 toll roads and bridges, and six power plants.
At the end of last year, CKI had committed HK$6.6 billion to 32 projects on the mainland.
CKI's future success lies firmly in China, said Li, the eldest son of Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd chairman Li Ka-shing.
"China is one of the fastest growing economies," he said. "This rapid growth gives rise to an urgent, massive demand for infrastructure investment."
Most Hong Kong participation in mainland infrastructural development projects in the past 10 years has been as financier, or the banker of last resort.
CKI aimed to do more, Li said, but did not give details on what that increased involvement might be.
"CKI is now a value-added investor firmly intertwined with our partners in their long-term development," said Li.
The company was not considering any overseas investment projects outside of China at this time, Li said.
As part of the restructuring of the Cheung Kong (Holdings) group that took effect from March, CKI has taken over Hutchison Whampoa Ltd's 35.01 percent stake in Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd.
CKI's earnings would continue to derive in large part from Hong Kong as a result.
